note.headline: Equities broaden and volatility eases while gold prints a record high
note.standfirst: The S&P 500 rose +0.44% to 7674.37 with financials and materials leading, and the VIX fell to 15.13 as breadth turned decisively positive. Gold's +3.22% rally to a record close alongside a crypto surge complicates a purely constructive read on the session's risk appetite.
takeaways: Breadth was strong, 16 advancers to 9 decliners, and the VIX fell -5.50% to 15.13, the surface reading of the tape.
Rotation favored cyclicals: financials and materials led while utilities fell -2.29% and megacap tech was mixed to soft.
Rates held completely still, with the curve and breakevens unchanged across every tenor.
Gold's +3.22% run to a record and bitcoin's +7.29% jump moved together, an unusual pairing that muddies the risk read.
note.desk_view:
The session confirms broad, cyclical participation: advancers beat decliners nearly 2 to 1, small caps outpaced megacap tech, and financials led on names like Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley. It also confirms a rates market in a holding pattern, with every tenor on the curve, and every point on the breakeven curve, printing unchanged.

What it does not confirm is a single, coherent story for gold. A +3.22% move to a record close, alongside a VIX at 15.13 and an equity tape up across the board, does not fit the metal's usual role as a fear hedge. The level that decides it: if gold keeps climbing while the 10-year holds 4.69% and TIPS breakevens stay pinned at 2.34%, the metals bid looks idiosyncratic and separate from the equity story. If gold instead starts trading opposite the S&P 500 again, that is the more familiar relationship reasserting itself, and it would argue for less conviction behind today's advance than the headline index level of 7674.37 suggests.
watching: Whether gold's advance past 4661.60 extends into a second session or fades back.
Whether the flat Treasury curve, 2s10s at 50bp, finally breaks in either direction.
Whether investment grade credit confirms fresh lows or the LQD move reverses.
Whether bitcoin holds today's close near 78355.71 or gives back the +7.29% gain.
note.equities:
The S&P 500 added +0.44% to close at 7674.37, with the Dow the best large-cap index at +0.98% to 53277.01. The Russell 2000 outpaced the Nasdaq 100, +0.85% against +0.33%, and mid-caps rose +0.51%. Breadth backed the tape: 16 advancers against 9 decliners, a 1.78 ratio, with dispersion at 1.51, moderate rather than extreme.

Materials led sectors at +2.14%, followed by health care +1.29% and consumer discretionary +1.15%. Financials rose +0.93%, with Goldman Sachs +3.73% and Morgan Stanley +3.25% pacing single names. Utilities was the session's clear loser at -2.29%, and energy slipped -0.17% as WTI fell -1.36%. Technology barely moved, +0.12%, weighed by Nvidia -0.98%, Apple -0.63% and Amazon -0.57%. Tesla was the top single mover at +5.14%, and Walmart printed among the session's lows.
note.rates:
The curve did not move. 2s10s held at 50bp, 5s30s at 84bp, 3m10y at 82bp, all unchanged on the session. Yield levels sat where they started: 2-year 4.19%, 5-year 4.39%, 10-year 4.69%, 30-year 5.23%.

Breakevens were equally still: 5-year and 10-year both at 2.34%, the 5y5y forward at 2.34%, and the 10-year TIPS real yield at 2.35%, none changed on the day. The MOVE index ticked up +0.30% to 73.40, a small divergence from the collapse in equity vol. Long Treasuries fell -0.35% and 7-10 year paper fell -0.19% to a session low, duration underperforming a flat yield tape.
note.credit: Investment grade lagged. LQD fell -0.13% and printed among the session's lows, while high yield firmed: HYG +0.06%, JNK +0.10%. Leveraged loans added +0.05% and EM sovereign debt rose +0.05%. The split, softer IG against a steady-to-firm HY and loan tape, reads as a duration story more than a credit-quality one.
note.fx: The dollar index slipped -0.06% to 98.839, a quiet session against a busier cross-rate board. The euro added +0.04%, sterling +0.35%, and the Swiss franc weakened +0.39% on a USD/CHF basis; the yen also gave ground, USD/JPY +0.37%. In EM, the peso and real firmed, USD/MXN -0.24% to a session low and USD/BRL -0.75%, while the lira weakened further, USD/TRY +0.19% to a fresh high, and the rupee eased, USD/INR +0.20%.
note.commodities: Crude diverged: WTI fell -1.36% to 86.64 while Brent held with a small +0.10% gain to 93.87, and natural gas rose +2.38%. Precious metals were the story of the day, gold +3.22% to 4661.60, a record close, with silver +1.45% and platinum +3.30%. Copper added +1.86% and aluminium +2.67% on the industrial side. Grains were firm, corn +6.16% to a fresh high and wheat +2.53%, but coffee fell -10.64%, the sharpest single move across the commodity complex.
note.volatility: The VIX fell -5.50% to 15.13 and VVIX dropped -4.00% to 86.27, a straightforward cheapening of equity protection. SKEW ticked up +0.47% to 143.90, tail cover holding a slight premium even as the front of the curve eased. The MOVE index rose +0.30% to 73.40, rates vol drifting the opposite direction from equity vol on the same session.
note.digital: Digital assets ran well ahead of every other risk asset. Bitcoin rose +7.29% to 78355.71, still down -11.69% on the year, and ether added +6.85%. Solana gained +6.74% and XRP led the majors at +10.83%. The move came against a dollar index that barely moved, -0.06%, a beta to risk well above anything else in the fact set.
note.international: Europe closed higher across the board: the EURO STOXX 50 added +0.63%, the DAX +0.59%, the FTSE 100 +0.64%, and the IBEX +0.76%, with the FTSE MIB essentially flat at +0.00%. Asian
